description:
PROBLEM TYPE: LP
PROBLEM INFO:

- A company is undergoing a number of changes that will affect its manpower requirements in future years. 
- Owing to the installation of new machinery, fewer unskilled but more skilled and semi-skilled workers will be required. 
- In addition to this, a downturn in trade is expected in the next year, which will reduce the need for workers in all categories.
- The estimated manpower requirements for manpower \var{k} in year \var{i} is \var{requirement_{k, i}}.
- The current number of manpower \var{k} is \var{strength_{k}}.
- The company wishes to decide its policy with regard to recruitment, retraining, redundancy and short-time working in the next years.
- There is a natural wastage of labour. 
- A fairly large number of workers leave during their first year. After this, the rate of leaving is much smaller. 
- Taking this into account, the wastage rates of manpower \var{k} with less than one year's service is \var{lessonewaste_{k}}.
- The wastage rates of \var{k} manpower with more than one year's service is \var{moreonewaste_{k}}.
- There has been no recent recruitment and all the workers in the current labour force have been employed for more than one year.
- It is possible to recruit a limited number of workers from outside. 
- In any one year, the maximum number that can be recruited in manpower \var{k} is \var{recruit_{k}}.
- The redundancy payment to manpower \var{k} is \var{costredundancy_{k}}.
- It is possible to employ up to \var{num_overman} more workers over the whole company than are needed, but the extra costs per employee per year is \var{costoverman_{k}} for manpower \var{k}.
- Up to \var{num_shortwork} workers in each category of skill can be put on short-time working. 
- The cost of this (per employee per year) is \var{costshort_{k}} for manpower \var{k}.
- An employee on short-time working meets the production requirements of half a full-time employee.


INPUT FORMAT:

{
    "requirement": [[requirement_{k, i} for i in 1,...,I] for k in 1,...,K],
    "strength": [strength_{k} for k in 1,...,K],
    "lessonewaste": [lessonewaste_{k} for k in 1,...,K],
    "moreonewaste": [lessonewaste_{k} for k in 1,...,K],
    "recruit": [recruit_{k} for k in 1,...,K],
    "costredundancy": [costredundancy_{k} for k in 1,...,K],
    "num_overman": num_overman,
    "costoverman": [costoverman_{k} for k in 1,...,K],
    "num_shortwork": num_shortwork
    "costshort": [costshort_{k} for k in 1,...,K],
}


OBJECTIVE: The company’s declared objective is to minimize redundancy. How should they operate in order to do this?

OUTPUT INFO:

- \var{recruit} represents the number of each recruit manpower to employ each year
- \var{overmanning} represents the number of each overmanning manpower to employ each year
- \var{short} represents the number of each short-time manpower to employ each year

OUTPUT FORMAT:

{
    "recruit": [[recruit_{k, i} for i in 1,...,I] for k in 1,...,K],
    "overmanning": [[overmanning_{k, i} for i in 1,...,I] for k in 1,...,K],
    "short": [[short_{k, i} for i in 1,...,I] for k in 1,...,K]
}

K.definition: Total number of different types of resources

I.definition: Number of different requirements for each type of resource

Strength.definition: Strength of each type of resource

LessOneWaste.definition: Value when wastage of resources is less than optimal

MoreOneWaste.definition: Value when wastage of resources is more than optimal

Recruit.definition: Number of recruited resources of each type

CostRedundancy.definition: Cost of redundancy for each type of resource

CostOverman.definition: Cost of overmanning for each type of resource

CostShort.definition: Cost of short working for each type of resource

Requirement.definition: Manpower requirements for each type of resource over the years

objective.description: "Minimize the total number of redundancies over the planning horizon"

constraints.description: For each manpower type k and year i, the workforce evolution must account for initial strength (in year 1), wastage of workers with less than one year of service at rate lessonewaste_k, wastage of workers with more than one year of service at rate moreonewaste_k, recruitment, and redundancies
constraints.formulation:
$\forall k:\; workforceMore[k,1] = (1 - MoreOneWaste[k]) \cdot Strength[k] - redundancies[k,1]$ 

$\forall k:\; workforceLess[k,1] = recruit[k,1]$ 

$\forall k,\; \forall i = 2,\dots,I:\; workforceMore[k,i] = (1 - MoreOneWaste[k]) \cdot workforceMore[k,i-1] + (1 - LessOneWaste[k]) \cdot workforceLess[k,i-1] - redundancies[k,i]$ 

$\forall k,\; \forall i = 2,\dots,I:\; workforceLess[k,i] = recruit[k,i]$

constraints.description: For each manpower type k, in year 1, the initial workforce is equal to the current strength, and all are treated as having more than one year of service
constraints.formulation: $\\forall k \\in \\{1,\\dots,K\\}: \\; workforceMore[k,1] + redundancies[k,1] = Strength[k] \\; \\land \\; workforceLess[k,1] = recruit[k,1]$

constraints.description: For each manpower type k and year i, the number of recruits cannot exceed recruit_k
For each manpower type k and year i, the number of workers put on short-time working cannot exceed num_shortwork
constraints.formulation: $\\forall k = 1, \\dots, K,\\; \\forall i = 1, \\dots, I:\\; short[k,i] \\leq NumShortwork$

constraints.description: For each manpower type k and year i, full-time workers plus 0.5 times short-time workers must equal requirement_{k,i} plus overmanning_{k,i}
For each year i, the total overmanning across all manpower types cannot exceed num_overman
Redundancies, recruitments, overmanning, and short-time working variables must be non-negative for all manpower types and years
constraints.formulation: $\\forall k = 1, \\dots, K, \\; \\forall i = 1, \\dots, I:\\; recruit_{k,i} \\ge 0, \\; redundancies_{k,i} \\ge 0, \\; overmanning_{k,i} \\ge 0, \\; short_{k,i} \\ge 0$

workforceMore.definition: Number of workers of type k in year i with more than one year of service after wastage and redundancies

workforceLess.definition: Number of workers of type k in year i with less than one year of service (new recruits)

recruit.definition: Number of newly recruited workers of type k in year i

redundancies.definition: Number of redundant workers of type k in year i

short.definition: Number of workers of type k put on short-time working in year i

overmanning.definition: Number of overmanning workers of type k in year i (workers employed in excess of requirement)
